e: Electricity is a form of energy. Energy here means the capacity to do work. Matter: anything that has mass and occupies space.

q: There are two types of electricity: electrostatics (or static electricity) and _____.
e: There are two types of electricity: electrostatics (or static electricity) and electrodynamics (or current electricity). Electrodynamics (or current electricity) here means the flow of electric charge.

q: Electrostatics is the study of electric charge at _____.
e: Electrostatics is the study of electric charge at rest. Electrostatics is charge at rest. Like charges push apart involving charge.

q: Electrodynamics is the study of moving electric charges and their interaction with magnetic and _____.
e: Electrodynamics is the study of moving electric charges and their interaction with magnetic and electric fields. The physics in this sentence is built around electric fields.

q: The two kinds of static electric charge are positive charge and _____.
e: The two kinds of static electric charge are positive charge and negative charge. Negative charge here means the electric property that makes objects attract or repel. Neutral charge: the electric property that makes objects attract or repel.

q: Benjamin Franklin named them positive charge which is represented by a plus sign (+) and negative charge by a _____.
e: Benjamin Franklin named them positive charge which is represented by a plus sign (+) and negative charge by a minus sign (-). The physics in this sentence is built around minus sign (-).

q: Like charges _____ and unlike charges attract.
e: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. The physics in this sentence is built around repel involving charges.

q: The electric force between two charged objects is one of the _____ forces of nature.
e: The electric force between two charged objects is one of the fundamental forces of nature. The physics in this sentence is built around fundamental involving charged.

q: In SI units, electric charge is measured in _____, in honour of Charles Augustin de Coulomb.
e: In SI units, electric charge is measured in coulomb (C), in honour of Charles Augustin de Coulomb. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: The magnitude of charge of an electron is _____.
e: The magnitude of charge of an electron is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C. The physics in this sentence is built around $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ C.

q: One coulomb of charge is equivalent to the charge of _____ electrons.
e: One coulomb of charge is equivalent to the charge of $6.25 \times 10^{18}$ electrons. The physics in this sentence is built around $6.25 \times 10^{18}$.

q: Charge is one of the _____ physical quantities.
e: Charge is one of the quantized physical quantities. The physics in this sentence is built around quantized involving quantities.

q: The formula for quantized charge is _____, where $n$ is an integer and $e$ is the charge of an electron.
e: The formula for quantized charge is $Q = ne$, where $n$ is an integer and $e$ is the charge of an electron. The physics in this sentence is built around $Q = ne$.

q: The unit of electric charge is named in honour of _____.
e: The unit of electric charge is named in honour of Charles Augustin de Coulomb. The unit that belongs with this quantity is Charles Augustin de Coulomb.
One microcoulomb ($1 \mu$C) is equal to $10^{-6}$ C. The physics in this sentence is built around $10^{-6}$ C.

q: The charge carrier of the conductor are _____.
e: The charge carrier of the conductor are electrons. A conductor has plenty of free electrons, so charge can move.

q: When an electron is removed from an atom, it becomes a _____ ion.
e: When an electron is removed from an atom, it becomes a positive ion. The physics in this sentence is built around positive.

q: There is an electric current in a conductor when electrons are _____.
e: There is an electric current in a conductor when electrons are moving. Current is charge passing a point per second.

q: A glass rod becomes positively charged when it is rubbed with silk because it _____.
e: A glass rod becomes positively charged when it is rubbed with silk because it loses electrons. The physics in this sentence is built around loses electrons.
